agree.reason: The letter's tone is measured, its three asks are modest, and the 74 signatures (two in three households) undercut her view that this is "a few loud people", but it leaves out the missed dialysis appointments, its strongest fact, so the cost of the outages stays abstract to a reader who thinks the company has done well.

honest.reason: Every figure traces to the brief and the derived ratios are fair, but "in an emergency, they have no safe way out" overstates things, since the building has stairs and elevators are not normally used in emergencies anyway.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the raw counts into "one day in every eight" and "two in every three" households, and it sets June against five months later, but it never shows that the June estimate of six to eight weeks pointed to August, so the part is now months overdue, and it drops the dialysis fact.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the status quo as a part promised since June that still hasn't come and an elevator that keeps failing, but it doesn't say what continuing this way means, such as more 12-day stretches or a repeat of this year's 41 days.

qualification.reason: Conceding that a second elevator "may" be impossible is honest, but the asks come with no reply deadline, no target date and no consequence if management misses one, so the reader has nothing to check.

objections.reason: It meets the passing inspection, the cost of a second elevator and the "few loud people" view head-on, and it raises no objection the facts already answer, but it leaves the obvious objection to a rent credit (cost and precedent) untouched.

fit.reason: It is a properly addressed open letter of about 420 words, dated the 1st of next month to match the posting date, and it is suitable both for the lobby and for the press.
